Reason: The chest X-ray report identifies the mediastinal and hilar contours as unchanged, and in the context of a foreign body case where symptoms were absent for years, this implies the object is located in the right hilum (the most common site for aspirated foreign bodies) and is aligned longitudinally with the bronchus to allow air passage; Option F correctly describes this high-density structure and the mechanism for its asymptomatic presentation.
